newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ship engine, locomotive maker plans layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Polish ship engine, locomotive maker plans layoffs.

text.p: The Polish state-owned ship engine and locomotive maker Zaklady Przemyslu Metalowego H. Cegielski SA will sack 200 out of its 5,300 employees by the end of 1996 because of financial problems, Cegielski's spokesman said.

Boleslaw Januszkiewicz told Reuters the group lay-offs were a result of dwindling orders for rolling stock from the Polish State Railways (PKP) and closures or problems of domestic and foreign shipyards to which Cegielski sold ship engines.

"Two hundred of Cegielski's employees, both from the ship engine and rolling-stock departments will lose jobs as a result of group lay-offs by the end of this year," he said, adding half of the dismissed were already eligible for retirement.

"The move is necessary, because orders from PKP have fallen this year and 1997 is uncertain. Also the bankruptcy of the Gdansk and Bremer Vulcan shipyards and problems of the Gdynia shipyard affected our production," Januszkiewicz said.
He said Cegielski would sell only between 72 and 74 percent of the ship engines it had expected to sell this year and the ship engine department generated some 60 percent of the company's profits.

He said Cegielski's standing would improve if it found a strategic investor for a majority stake in its rolling-stock department, because it could then enter PKP tenders against the competition of the Wroclaw-based Pafawag about-to-be bought by Germany's Adtranz.
"We are in talks with several serious western companies," he said, but declined to give any further details.
Januszkiewicz said Cegielski had a net profit of 887,000 zlotys in 1995 on a gross profit of 7.61 million zlotys on sales of 15.3 million zlotys.
